title: Target anatomy
view: Oblique section of the right anterior chest wall at the 3rd-4th rib level under a linear probe: lateral (the axilla) on the image left, medial on the right, skin at the top.
teachingPoint: PECS I between pectoralis major and minor; PECS II one plane deeper, between pectoralis minor and serratus anterior - stop there, short of the ribs and pleura.
claims: Right chest wall in section, lateral on the left, the same way round as the positioning plate.
Upper teal: PECS I, the plane between pectoralis major and minor (record), with the pectoral branch of the thoracoacromial artery in it (standard).
Lower teal: PECS II, the pectoserratus plane between pectoralis minor and serratus anterior (record).
Needle in-plane from medial (right) through pectoralis major and minor, tip in the PECS II plane, above serratus, ribs and pleura (record).
Labels: Pectoralis major, Pectoralis minor, Serratus anterior, PECS I, PECS II.

geometry.why: PECS II is the deeper plane
tip in the PECS II plane
in-plane from the medial end (medial is right)
the artery marks the PECS I plane
